purpose: Per CEO R283 P2: 'BOM → assembly drawings → control code → calibration procedure → attack-generation procedure → blinded randomization → raw-data schema → analysis script → acceptance criteria. The external lab should be able to run it without asking us how to interpret the result.'
constitutional_basis: Article XXVI — independent validation. Article XXX — bench must be able to disprove simulator.

1_bom.components_summary: Heated reservoir, pulsatile pump, 4-segment acrylic manifold, 4× variable orifice valves (Takasago RK-1), 4× programmable occlusion resistors (stepper+clamp), 4× flow sensors (Sensirion SLF3S), proximal pressure sensor (Honeywell ABP2), DAQ (NI USB-6210 or LabJack T7), controller PC
1_bom.vendors: All commercial off-the-shelf. No custom fabrication except acrylic manifold (Protolabs or 3D print).

2_assembly_drawings.schematic: [CSF Reservoir 37°C] → [Pulsatile Pump] → [Proximal Pressure Sensor] → [4-way Manifold] → 4× [Segment: Flow Sensor → Variable Orifice Valve → Programmable Occlusion Resistor] → [Distal Reservoir]
2_assembly_drawings.wiring: Sensors → DAQ analog inputs (0-5V). DAQ digital outputs → valve drivers. Controller PC → DAQ via USB.
2_assembly_drawings.physical_layout: Bench-top, 60cm × 40cm × 30cm acrylic frame. All components accessible for maintenance.
2_assembly_drawings.full_drawings_status: TO BE PRODUCED when buyer commits to building (CAD files: SolidWorks or Fusion 360)

3_control_code.dependencies: None (pure Python, no external libraries for controller logic)
3_control_code.bench_integration: Controller reads sensor data from DAQ (CSV or real-time stream), outputs valve commands to DAQ. Same algorithm as simulator.

steps: 1. Pressure sensor calibration: Apply known hydrostatic pressure (water column). Verify reading within ±0.5 mmHg across 0-30 mmHg range.
2. Flow sensor calibration: Pump known flow rate through each sensor. Verify within ±0.05 mL/min across 0-0.5 mL/min range.
3. Valve calibration: Command 0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100%. Measure effective conductance at each. Fit calibration curve (R² > 0.95).
4. Occlusion resistor calibration: Command 0-100% closure. Measure conductance reduction. Verify reproducibility ±2%.
5. Pump calibration: Measure output volume over 1 hour. Verify within ±5% of setpoint (0.30 mL/min).
6. Temperature stability: Monitor water bath over 24 hours. Verify 37°C ± 0.5°C.
7. Leak test: Pressurize to 20 mmHg, all valves closed. Verify pressure drop < 1 mmHg over 1 hour.
8. DAQ timing: Generate 1 Hz signal on all channels. Verify timestamps align within ±10 ms.
4_calibration_procedure.frequency: Full calibration before each test campaign. Quick checks (steps 1, 5, 7) before each run.
4_calibration_procedure.pass_criteria: All calibration checks must pass before formal validation begins.

all_9_attacks.name: none
all_9_attacks.method: Run with default parameters, no disturbances

all_9_attacks.name: noise_3x
all_9_attacks.method: Software adds 3x Gaussian noise to sensor readings before controller

all_9_attacks.name: sensor_dropout
all_9_attacks.method: Software sets sensor readings to 0 for 60s, every 5-15 min (randomized)

all_9_attacks.name: fast_occlusion
all_9_attacks.method: Programmable resistor closes 5x faster than default (full closure ~12 min vs 60 min)

all_9_attacks.name: slow_occlusion
all_9_attacks.method: Programmable resistor closes 5x slower (full closure ~5 hours)

all_9_attacks.name: wrong_model
all_9_attacks.method: Controller assumes exponential decay; actual resistor closure is linear

all_9_attacks.name: controller_delay
all_9_attacks.method: Software adds 5-second delay between controller output and valve command

5_attack_generation_procedure.implementation: All attacks SOFTWARE-INJECTED via DAQ/controller. No hardware reconfiguration between attacks.

procedure: 1. Randomization script (Python, seed recorded) generates test sequence: 3 arms (A/B/C) × 9 attacks × 5 seeds = 135 runs, randomly ordered
2. Script encrypts arm identity using AES-256 with passphrase held by third party
3. Controller PC loads encrypted config at start of each run. Analyst sees only 'Run 001', 'Run 002', etc.
4. Analyst sets up attack parameters, starts run, records data — without knowing which controller is active
5. After all 135 runs, third party reveals passphrase
6. Results unblinded and compared to simulator predictions
6_blinded_randomization.integrity: Cryptographic blinding. Analyst cannot influence which arm runs.

per_run_files: run_XXX_metadata.json — arm (encrypted), attack, seed, timestamp, calibration status
run_XXX_summary.json — computed metrics (t_fail, peak, drainage, etc.)
7_raw_data_schema.format: CSV for time-series (standard, universally readable). JSON for metadata and summaries.
7_raw_data_schema.storage: ~50 MB per run, ~7 GB for full 135-run validation

8_analysis_script.function: Reads raw CSV data, computes 8 metrics per run, compares to simulator predictions, generates comparison report
8_analysis_script.input: Raw CSV files from bench runs
8_analysis_script.output: JSON summary + markdown report with simulator-vs-bench comparison
8_analysis_script.falsification_check: If bench results differ from simulator by >30% on any metric, flags as SIMULATOR FALSIFICATION event

criteria: BC-01: V2.1 peak ICP under noise_3x <= 25 mmHg (simulator: 19.5)
BC-05: All metrics within ±30% of simulator prediction (else SIMULATOR IS WRONG)
9_acceptance_criteria.rule: Cannot be silently relaxed (Article XXVII). If bench disagrees with simulator by >30%, the simulator is revised, not the bench.

what_external_lab_receives: All 9 sections above. The lab can procure, build, calibrate, run, and analyze WITHOUT asking us how to interpret results.
